findings.title: The comparison's general conclusions and several coverage descriptions need correction
findings.reproduction: Read the full comparison against its own qualifications and the actual old/current Lean definitions BatchProgram.Program/run/execution, G7.bound, WalletSelection.chosen_eq/actual_eq, G4/G5 guards and G10NoWallet.bound.
findings.expected: The summary preserves hypotheses and model differences, and coverage claims credit existing batch and selection-law bridges.
findings.observed: The document already honestly discloses many restrictions, including non-comparable genuine-record kernels, yet concludes broadly that the same theorems are proved. It says no batch game exists and selection rules are not connected, omits no-Early guards from its G4/G5 summary, and leaves a no-wallet correspondence cell blank despite crediting that theorem elsewhere.
findings.impact: Readers can overestimate experiment equivalence and underestimate particular checked Lean bridges. These are errors in the comparison, not counterexamples to the audited security inequalities.
findings.evidence: Complete independent rereading by coordinator and two specialist scopes; historical snapshot and current source traces in the embedded annexes; baseline proof validity in AUD-011/AUD-012.
findings.recommendedFix: Retain the detailed comparison and its honest limitations, correct the concrete coverage/guard/table descriptions, and replace the blanket conclusion with agreement of core bounds under their respective explicitly listed premises.
findings.requiredVerification: Each revised coverage statement identifies the actual final event, inherited hypotheses and law/program bridge; the summary agrees with the detailed qualification table and dated source manifests.

findings.title: The port account retains stale theorem-presence, patch-size and checkpoint-path claims
findings.affected: PORT-v4.35.md declaration/inventory, size and Checkpoint descriptions; tools/decls.py and decldiff.py evidence interpretation.
findings.reproduction: Regenerate the three declaration TSVs, inspect both inventories and the actual source diff, and compare GNU diff counts and Checkpoint's current output path with the account.
findings.expected: Intentional removals are explicit exceptions to universal presence claims; patch counts and paths bind to the actual reviewed artifact; textual headers are not described as complete semantic evidence.
findings.observed: The reproduced header counts are correct, but two intentionally removed K5 helper theorems contradict 'Every theorem ... is present'. Claimed 618 additions/380 deletions differs from retained 660/382 and current GNU 661/384; current Checkpoint writes to cwd. The parser omits context, definition bodies and modifiers, and has demonstrated lexical limitations.
findings.impact: The publication narrative and reproducibility evidence disagree. No additional unintended mathematical change or false current bound was identified; the parser's limits do not establish a hidden real-port discrepancy.
findings.evidence: Byte-identical reproduction of snapshot.tsv, port.tsv and diff.tsv; 12 public textual parser probes; inspected finite-answer class migration, restored PMF definitions and actual current patch.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the two-helper exception, regenerate/date the patch statistics and relative checkpoint path, and state that the parser compares normalized textual headers. Preserve the independently reviewed mathematical interpretation and intended K5/W5 changes.
findings.requiredVerification: Current counts/paths match their retained artifacts; all 40 current modules retain AUD-012 validity; semantic claims cite definition/context review rather than only header counts.
